topic.title: Salary credited at 10 am.
topic.claim: Young Indians saying they'd rather spend on a wellness retreat than a branded bag aren't rejecting status spending, they're just doing status spending that doesn't photograph as a logo anymore.
topic.behaviour: Under-40 buyers account for 60% of India's luxury purchases versus 40% globally, Gen Z drives about 47% of fashion-and-lifestyle spend, and professionals still put 15-20% of income into premium products while increasingly prioritising travel and wellness over owning branded goods.
topic.mechanism: A watch or a bag used to be the visible marker of status, now the visible marker is a story, a reel from a retreat, a boarding pass, so the spend hasn't dropped, only the format of the flex has changed.
topic.group: Urban professionals in their 20s and 30s with disposable luxury spending power
topic.news_peg: Report on young Indians shifting luxury spending toward experiences, October 2026
topic.why_now: Published this month amid festive and wedding-season luxury spending

score.why: Fits her 'wellness is marketing wearing a yoga mat' belief exactly: it's still status spending, just repackaged so it doesn't photograph as a logo.

topic.send_to: the friend who just posted from a retreat in the hills

edits: slide 1: Shorten the opener to 'Skipping the branded bag for a wellness retreat isn't giving up status. You just moved it.' It's easier to read in one go.
slide 1: Cut 'The flex just stopped needing a logo.' It repeats the opener and reads as a tidy punchline. End on 'The spend didn't drop.'
slide 1: Change 'premium stuff' to 'premium products', which is the wording in the source figure. Optionally add one short reaction from her, such as 'Honestly, the retreat reel is the louder flex.'

paragraphs: Skipping the branded bag for a wellness retreat isn't giving up status. You just moved it.
A logo used to do the showing off. Now a reel from a retreat in the hills does it. So does a boarding pass on your story.
Professionals still put 15-20% of income into premium products. The spend didn't drop.

replaced_after_panel_review.caption: The logo didn't disappear. It moved to the boarding pass.
replaced_after_panel_review.alt_text: A single text slide arguing that young Indians choosing wellness retreats over branded bags are still spending on status. The showing off has moved from logos to reels and boarding passes, and professionals still put 15-20% of their income into premium products.

claims.text: Professionals still allocate 15-20% of income to premium products
Younger affluent Indian consumers are prioritising experiences over product ownership, with wellness becoming a status marker

paragraphs: By 2 pm, the rent, two EMIs, the SIP and the credit card bill have each taken their share.
You were rich for four hours.
